RESIDENTIAL DWELLING INSURANCE
GENERAL POLICY CONDITIONS - PROPERTY DAMAGE COVER
Policy wording "WD-2026" - Break-in Damage to the Building Edition

These conditions apply together with the General Contract Provisions and with
the Schedule, both of which form part of this contract. Sums insured, limits,
deductibles, periods and percentages shown in square brackets are those stated
in the Schedule.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - PURPOSE AND KEY CONCEPTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 What this insurance does

Combined residential buildings insurance protects the policyholder against the
financial consequences of physical damage to their building. The perils that can
be insured are the ones bundled together in these conditions - fire, escape of
water, storm and hail, further natural hazards, and damage to the building caused
by breaking in among them. Which of the insurable perils are actually covered is
agreed between insurer and policyholder and recorded in the schedule.

Where insured property is destroyed or damaged, the insurer indemnifies the cost
of putting it back, on an index-linked reinstatement basis with an enhancement. A
range of consequential expenses triggered by a loss event is also carried, within
the limits agreed for each head.

This is a buildings contract. What it insures is the building, the things built
into it and the things that serve it. The movable property kept inside it, and
the movable property of the household generally, is the subject of a separate
contract. An event may damage both; this contract answers only for the part of
that damage which falls on the building.

1.2 How the wording is to be read

Personal designations are to be understood as gender-neutral throughout; no
parallel male and female forms are used.

1.3 Explanation of recurring terms (not legally binding)

Policyholder - the insurer's contracting party and the purchaser of the cover.

Insured event - the event for which the insurer pays.

Exclusion - a peril, a type of damage or an item of property for which no cover
exists. Exclusions delimit what has been promised and keep the cover calculable.

Affected part or item - a room, surface, building component, fitting or
installation on which physical damage caused by the insured event is established
by the loss investigation.

Repair cost - the outlay directed at making good the physical damage caused by
the insured event on an affected part or item of insured property. Outlay
directed at property that is not insured under this contract is not a repair cost
under it, whatever its connection with the same event.

Ancillary charge - any charge raised alongside the itemised labour and materials:
call-out and travel, carriage and dispatch, assembly and fitting, small parts and
consumables, disposal, administration, handling and comparable items. An
ancillary charge shares the fate of the work it accompanies.

Duties - the things the policyholder must do or refrain from doing before, during
and after an insured event.

Secured lenders - creditors whose claim is secured by a charge registered against
the property. The interests of secured lenders enjoy statutory protection.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - INSURED PERILS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 The perils that can be covered

The insurer indemnifies insured property that is destroyed or damaged by, or lost
as a consequence of, the following events:

  (a) FIRE GROUP - fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning;
      explosion; deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft, its
      parts or its cargo; impact of a vehicle; scorching; smoke and soot.

  (b) ESCAPE OF WATER.

  (c) NATURAL HAZARDS, in two tiers:
        (c1) storm and hail;
        (c2) the further natural hazards - flood, backing-up of water,
             earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and
             volcanic eruption.

  (d) BREAK-IN DAMAGE TO THE BUILDING.

2.2 How the groups combine

Each of the groups (a), (b), (c1) and (d) can be taken separately. The further
natural hazards under (c2) can only be taken in combination with one or more of
the perils in (a), (b) or (c1).

2.3 The fire group defined

2.3.1 Fire is a combustion that has started without a hearth intended for it, or
that has escaped such a hearth, and that is capable of spreading under its own
power. Lightning strike is the direct passage of a lightning discharge onto
property. Overvoltage caused by lightning covers damage through overvoltage,
overcurrent or short circuit in insured electrical installations and appliances.

2.3.2 Explosion and deflagration are suddenly running force events resting on the
tendency of gases or vapours to expand; implosion is a sudden collapse of a
hollow body under external overpressure.

2.3.3 The impact or crash of an aircraft, its parts or its cargo is covered, as
is the impact of a road, rail or water-borne vehicle, save where its keeper or
driver is the policyholder or an occupant of the building.

2.3.4 Scorch damage arising out of one of the events above is covered; scorch
damage from any other cause up to [amount]. Smoke and soot damage arising out of
one of those events is covered; damage from the gradual action of smoke or soot
is not.

2.3.5 Not covered within this group is damage caused by earthquake; damage to
internal combustion engines from explosions inside the combustion chamber; and
damage at the switching elements of electrical switches from the gas pressure
inside them, unless the consequence of an insured fire event.

2.4 Escape of water defined

2.4.1 The escape of water peril covers damage caused by escaping water, fracture
damage to insured pipework inside buildings, and fracture damage to insured
pipework outside buildings.

2.4.2 Escaping water means water that has emerged, contrary to its intended
purpose, from a water-carrying installation situated on the insured site.

2.4.3 Not covered is damage caused by splash or cleaning water; by dry rot and
house-rot fungi; by groundwater, surface water, flood, precipitation or a
backing-up brought about by these; by earthquake, snow load, avalanche or
volcanic eruption; by ground subsidence or landslip not caused by escaping water;
by the perils of the fire group; by the opening of sprinklers on account of fire,
pressure testing or works; or by storm or hail.

2.5 Natural hazards defined

2.5.1 Storm means a weather-driven movement of air reaching at least the gale
threshold on the recognised scale of wind strength; hail means solid
precipitation in the form of grains of ice. Only damage arising from the direct
action of storm or hail on insured property, or on buildings structurally joined
to it, is covered, together with damage caused by objects thrown onto them.

2.5.2 The further natural hazards are flood, backing-up of water, earthquake,
ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and volcanic eruption, each as
customarily defined.

2.5.3 Not covered is damage caused by storm surge; by the penetration of
precipitation or dirt through openings that were not properly closed; by
groundwater save where it emerged at the surface as a result of precipitation or
overflow; by the perils of the fire group, save where triggered by an insured
earthquake; and by drought or desiccation.

2.6 Break-in damage to the building defined

2.6.1 What the peril is
Covered is the physical damage caused to insured property where a person breaks
into, forces open, breaks out of, or attempts by comparable means to enter or
leave, the insured building, a part of it, or a locked receptacle firmly
connected with it.

Covered equally is the damage caused where a person opens the building or a part
of it using a key or code obtained through an insured event under this heading or
by force against a person, and the damage caused where the building is entered
through an opening created for that purpose.

2.6.2 What the indemnity comprises
The indemnity comprises the making good of the affected fabric and fittings of
the building: doors and door leaves, frames, thresholds and surrounds; windows,
shutters, grilles and their frames; locks, cylinders, escutcheons, handles,
hinges, bolts, closers and comparable hardware; the associated glazing; the
affected wall, ceiling and floor surfaces and finishes; the affected fixed
installations of the building; and the enclosures, gates and barriers on the
insured site insofar as they are insured property.

Where a lock or a locking system has been damaged, opened or compromised, the
indemnity comprises its replacement and, where the compromised element forms part
of a system, the re-keying or replacement of the further elements of that system
that are necessary to restore its security.

Securing the building provisionally until the permanent repair can be carried out
is covered under 5.2.1.

2.6.3 What the peril does not comprise
This peril does not indemnify the taking of property, nor damage to property that
is not insured under this contract. Where movable property was taken, damaged or
destroyed in the course of the same event, that loss falls outside this contract
in its entirety (4.3), together with the whole of the outlay directed at it
(7.1.8(a)).

2.6.4 Damage excluded within this peril
Not covered:
  (a) damage caused by a person who lives in the insured building, who is
      employed in the household, or to whom access was entrusted, save where that
      person obtained access by an act falling within 2.6.1;
  (b) damage caused by opening the building with a key or code that was properly
      in the possession of the person using it;
  (c) damage discovered only on a later occasion and not attributable to an
      identified event;
  (d) the replacement or upgrading of locks, hardware or security equipment on
      parts of the building which the event did not reach, and the strengthening
      of the building's security beyond the standard in place before the event
      (3.1.6, 7.1.9).


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - EXCLUSIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 General exclusions

3.1.1 War
Damage caused by war, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or
insurrection is not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.2 Civil commotion
Damage caused by internal civil unrest is not covered, irrespective of any
contributing causes.

3.1.3 Nuclear energy
Damage caused by nuclear energy, nuclear radiation or radioactive substances is
not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.4 Liability risks
Claims of third parties against the policyholder, and any outlay directed at
covering, assessing, administering or settling such claims, are not the subject
of this contract.

3.1.5 Property outside this contract
Loss of, damage to, and every measure directed at property that is not insured
under Part 4 is outside this contract. This applies irrespective of whether the
property was damaged in the same event as the insured property, whether the
measure was carried out at the same time as covered work, whether it was
necessary to restore the household to its former state, and whether the
policyholder holds other insurance in respect of it. Where such property is
insured elsewhere, the claim belongs to that contract.

3.1.6 Upkeep, improvement and precautionary measures
Outlay directed at the servicing, maintenance, cleaning, general condition,
modernisation or improvement of property, and the renewal of a part or item on
which no damage from the insured event has been established, is not
indemnifiable, even where the measure is taken as a precaution or on a technical
recommendation.

3.2 Exclusions within the fire group

See 2.3.5.

3.3 Exclusions within the escape of water peril

See 2.4.3.

3.4 Exclusions within the natural hazards

See 2.5.3.

3.5 Exclusions within the break-in peril

See 2.6.3 and 2.6.4.

3.6 Work beyond the affected parts, and outlay that is not a repair cost

Work carried out beyond those parts and items of the insured property that were
themselves affected by the insured event is not covered. Outlay that does not
constitute a repair cost is not indemnified. The delimitation in each case is
governed by 7.1.5 to 7.1.10.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - INSURED PROPERTY, INSURED LOCATION, DEDUCTIBLES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 What is insured

Insured property comprises the buildings identified in the schedule, their
building components, their building accessories, terraces on the insured site
that directly adjoin the building, and further site installations named in the
schedule.

4.2 The categories defined

4.2.1 Building and dwelling
Buildings are structures connected to the ground, capable of affording protection
against external influences and intended for predominantly residential use.
Garages, sheds, stores, cellars, bicycle and bin stores and comparable ancillary
structures count as insured property insofar as they stand on the insured site
and are named in the schedule. Their contents do not.

4.2.2 Building components
Items incorporated into a building that have lost their independence through
their firm connection with it, together with the fitting-out elements of the
dwelling: floor coverings with their bedding and underlay; wall and ceiling
finishes; interior and exterior doors, windows and their frames; and fixed trim,
skirting, beading and comparable edging elements.

4.2.3 Building accessories
Movable items located inside the building or attached to its exterior which serve
the upkeep of the insured building or its predominant intended purpose - among
them the locking, closing, access and security equipment belonging to it, its
bell and letterbox installations, and its bin and store enclosures.

Items which serve the personal use, transport, recreation, sport or leisure of
the occupants do not serve the upkeep of the building or its intended purpose,
and are not building accessories, wherever they are kept and however habitually
they are kept there.

4.2.4 Building services installations
The electrical, water, heating, air-conditioning, ventilation and comparable
technical installations serving the building are insured property insofar as they
serve the building itself and are not excluded under 4.3.

4.2.5 Terraces and further site installations
Terraces are paved surfaces intended for occupation in the open air. Further site
installations are the items firmly connected with the ground and soil of the
insured site listed in the schedule, including the enclosures, gates and barriers
named there.

4.3 Property not insured

Not insured:
  (a) the movable property of the household and the personal effects of the
      occupants, whether kept in the dwelling, in an ancillary room, in a store,
      in a garage or elsewhere on the insured site;
  (b) means of transport of every kind, whether motorised, electrically assisted
      or propelled by muscle power, together with their frames, bodies, wheels,
      drives, braking, steering and control assemblies, batteries, trailers,
      carriers and all further parts and accessories, and together with the
      equipment used with them;
  (c) sports, leisure, hobby and recreational equipment and its parts and
      accessories;
  (d) tools, machines, appliances and equipment kept for the personal use of the
      occupants rather than for the upkeep of the building;
  (e) photovoltaic installations and their components, including a permanently
      connected electricity storage installation;
  (f) items subsequently incorporated into the building by a tenant or by a
      condominium owner at that person's own expense and at that person's own
      risk, unless co-insured under 4.4;
  (g) electronically stored data and programs;
  (h) property acquired on the occasion of the loss which does not replace an
      affected item of insured property of the same kind and intended purpose.

The exclusion of an item under this clause extends to everything done to it and
for it: its repair, the replacement of its parts and assemblies, the labour hours
of every grade spent on that work, the components, small parts and consumables
consumed by it, its assembly, fitting, adjustment and testing, its carriage and
dispatch, and the attendance charge of the trade that carried the work out
(7.1.8(a)).

4.4 Optionally insurable

Items subsequently incorporated by a tenant or condominium owner can be
co-insured where this is agreed. The movable property of the household can be
insured under a separate contract; it does not become insured property under this
one by reason of being damaged in the same event.

4.5 The insured location

The insured location is the insured site: the land parcel or parcels on which the
insured building stands.

4.6 Condominium and part-ownership units

Where the contract is with an association of condominium owners and the insurer
is wholly or partly released from liability on account of the conduct of
individual owners, it remains obliged to pay the remaining owners in respect of
their separate property and their shares in the common property. The remaining
owners may claim indemnity for the co-ownership share concerned where the
additional indemnity is applied to reinstating the common property; the owner
concerned must reimburse the insurer. These provisions apply correspondingly to
part-ownership units.

4.7 Deductibles

A deductible is the share of the indemnity, or the amount, that the policyholder
bears itself per insured event. Deductibles can be agreed individually and may
differ from one insured peril and one insured benefit to another. Each is set out
in the schedule. The deductible is applied once per insured event to the covered
settlement, irrespective of the number of trades or invoices involved.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - INSURED COSTS, LOSS OF RENT AND RENTAL VALUE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Which costs are covered

The insurer reimburses the following costs where they were necessary as a
consequence of an insured event and were actually incurred:
  (a) emergency and mitigation measures, including the provisional securing and
      closing of the building;
  (b) debris removal and disposal costs;
  (c) costs of moving and protecting insured property;
  (d) hotel costs;
  (e) costs of returning early from a holiday.

Reimbursement of each of these heads is limited to the amount agreed for it. This
list is exhaustive.

5.2 The cost heads defined

5.2.1 Emergency and mitigation measures
Costs of the measures taken during or immediately after the insured event to
close, secure and make safe the building and to prevent the damage from
increasing - boarding, provisional locking, temporary closure of an opening and
comparable measures - capped at [amount] per insured event. These measures are
covered whether they are carried out by the trade that later performs the
permanent repair or by another.

5.2.2 Debris removal and disposal
Costs incurred in clearing away, removing and disposing of the material taken out
in the course of the covered works, including transport to the nearest disposal
site. This head is reimbursed once per insured event for the material concerned.

5.2.3 Moving and protecting property
Costs incurred in moving, altering or protecting property, where those measures
serve to reinstate or replace insured property.

5.2.4 Hotel costs
Costs of accommodation where the dwelling permanently occupied by the
policyholder has become uninhabitable and confining themselves to a habitable
part of it cannot reasonably be expected, reimbursed only to the extent that they
exceed the indemnity payable for rental value and only where indemnity cannot be
claimed under another insurance contract, up to [amount] per day for a maximum of
[number] days.

5.2.5 Early return from holiday
Additional travel costs arising because the policyholder, or a person living with
them in the same household, breaks off a holiday trip prematurely on account of a
significant insured event, in a reasonable amount and capped at [amount] per
insured event.

5.3 Loss of rent and rental value

The insurer reimburses loss of rent where tenants of residential premises have
lawfully stopped paying rent or terminated the tenancy on account of an insured
event, and the locally customary rental value of residential premises occupied by
the policyholder itself where use cannot reasonably be expected, in each case
including the running service charges in the sense of tenancy law.

5.4 The period for loss of rent and rental value

Loss of rent or rental value is reimbursed for the period during which the rooms
are unusable, but for no longer than [number] months from the occurrence of the
insured event, and only to the extent that the policyholder has not culpably
delayed the resumption of use.

5.5 Commercially used premises

For commercially used premises, insurance of loss of rent or of the locally
customary rental value can be agreed.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 6 - BASIS OF COVER AND PREMIUM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 Insurable value

The insurable value forms the basis for calculating the indemnity. The insurable
value determined for the building applies equally to building components,
building accessories, terraces and further site installations.

6.2 Index-linked reinstatement value with enhancement

6.2.1 What is insured is the locally customary new-build value of the buildings
identified in the schedule, taken at the time of the insured event. Architects'
fees and other construction and planning costs form part of that value.

6.2.2 Two elements are built into that value: additional costs arising from
public-law restrictions on reinstatement, and price increases arising between the
occurrence of the insured event and reinstatement initiated without delay.

6.2.3 The insurer tracks the cover under 6.2.1 against the development of
building costs.

6.2.4 The basis of cover determines the standard to which the affected parts and
items of insured property are put back. It does not bring property outside Part 4
into the cover, it does not extend the indemnity to parts the event did not
reach, and it does not fund a standard above the one in place before the loss.

6.3 Index-linked current value with enhancement where reinstatement is omitted or
    delayed

For buildings that are not reinstated, or are reinstated late, only the
index-linked current value with enhancement is insured - the enhanced new-build
value at the time of the insured event, less depreciation for age and wear.

6.4 Market value for permanently devalued buildings

For buildings designated for demolition, or otherwise permanently devalued, only
the achievable sale price excluding the land share is insured.

6.5 How the premium is calculated

The bases for calculating the premium are the area, the building type, the
construction and fit-out, the use, other agreed features material to the premium
calculation, and the adjustment factor.

6.6 Adjustment of cover and premium

Where cover is adjusted, the premium changes accordingly. The adjustment factor
changes with effect from 1 January of each year in line with the movement of a
construction price index for residential buildings and a collectively agreed wage
index for the construction sector, weighted as agreed and rounded to two decimal
places.

6.7 Subsequent change in a premium-rating feature

Where a rating circumstance subsequently changes and a higher premium results,
the insurer may demand the higher premium from the point at which the change is
notified. Where such a circumstance ceases to apply and a lower premium results,
the insurer must reduce the premium from the point at which it becomes aware of
that.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 7 - CALCULATION AND PAYMENT OF THE INDEMNITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 Basis of calculation

7.1.1 The insurer reimburses:
  (a) for destroyed buildings - the locally customary reinstatement costs at the
      time of the insured event;
  (b) for damaged buildings and other damaged insured property - the necessary
      repair costs at the time of the insured event, together with any diminution
      in value the repair does not offset, capped at the insurable value;
  (c) for destroyed or lost insured property other than buildings - the
      replacement price for property of the same kind and quality in new
      condition at the time of the insured event.

7.1.2 Where technically still usable substance may not be used for reinstatement
because of public-law requirements, the policyholder receives corresponding
indemnity, provided the orders in question were not already in force before the
insured event.

7.1.3 Price increases occurring between the insured event and reinstatement are
indemnified where reinstatement is secured within three years.

7.1.4 The achievable sale price of remains is set off in calculating the
indemnity.

7.1.5 Extent of the repair
Indemnity is confined to those parts and items of the insured property that were
themselves affected by the insured event, as established by the loss
investigation. Work carried out on a room, surface, component, item or
installation that was not itself affected is not covered, even where it is
carried out so that treated and untreated parts correspond in appearance; for
reasons of convenience or economy; as a precaution against a future event; at the
same time as covered work or in the course of it; or by the same contractor as
the covered work and invoiced together with it.

Where the affected element forms part of a locking or closing system whose
security depends on the integrity of the whole, the further elements of that
system are treated as affected to the extent necessary to restore that security
(2.6.2).

7.1.6 Continuous surfaces
Where only part of a single continuous surface was affected, indemnity extends to
the adjoining unaffected sections of that same surface only where a corresponding
replacement material is no longer obtainable and a visible discontinuity would
otherwise remain.

7.1.7 What the repair cost comprises
The necessary repair costs under 7.1.1(b) include, insofar as they are directed
at affected insured property:
  (a) taking down, dismantling, removing and disposing of the affected components
      and fittings;
  (b) the preparation of the substrate, frame, rebate or supporting structure
      before the replacement is fitted, and the making good of the surrounding
      surfaces and finishes disturbed by that work;
  (c) replacement components, fittings and hardware of a type, quality, grade and
      specification corresponding to those in place immediately before the
      insured event;
  (d) the assembly, fitting, installation, hanging, adjustment, alignment and
      functional testing of those replacement components in the building, this
      being part of the repair of a building component and not a separate supply
      service;
  (e) the labour hours needed for that work, at every grade of personnel employed
      on it - skilled, qualified, assisting, apprenticed and trainee alike - at
      the rates customary in the trade concerned, with the hours of each grade
      stated separately;
  (f) the small parts, fixings, sealing and comparable sundry materials and
      consumables incorporated into the work, whether itemised individually or
      collected under a single sundry heading;
  (g) one attendance at the insured location by each trade performing
      indemnifiable work, charged as a call-out, travel or vehicle item;
  (h) the final cleaning of the working area on completion of the covered works.

7.1.8 Outlay that is not a repair cost
The following do not constitute repair costs and are not indemnified, however
they may be described, bundled or invoiced, by whichever trade they are raised,
and irrespective of whether they appear on an invoice that also contains covered
work:

  (a) every measure directed at property that is not insured under Part 4 (3.1.5)
      - its repair, the replacement of its parts and assemblies, the labour hours
      of every grade spent on it, the components, small parts, sundries and
      consumables used on it, its assembly, fitting, adjustment and testing, its
      carriage and dispatch, and the attendance charge of the trade that carried
      that work out. Where an invoice is directed at such property, no line on it
      becomes indemnifiable by reason of being described in the same terms as a
      line that would be indemnifiable on the invoice of a trade working on the
      building;

  (b) measures directed at the servicing, maintenance, cleaning, general
      condition, tidiness, upkeep, modernisation or improvement of property, as
      distinct from making good the damage caused by the insured event, and the
      renewal of a part or item on which no damage from the event has been
      established (3.1.6);

  (c) the strengthening of the building's security beyond the standard in place
      immediately before the event, and the fitting of additional locking,
      closing, monitoring or alarm equipment (2.6.4(d), 7.1.9);

  (d) carriage, freight, delivery, dispatch, packaging, postage, courier,
      transport and comparable charges for bringing property to the insured
      location, whether raised by the supplier of that property or by a third
      party, and whether stated as a separate line, as a percentage or as a flat
      rate;

  (e) outlay belonging to a contractor's own business operation rather than to
      the repair - its own tools, plant and consumable small equipment as such,
      its own diagnostic and measuring devices, provisioning, catering and
      comparable subsistence for its own personnel, and general administrative,
      handling, order-processing or documentation charges levied in addition to
      itemised labour and materials;

  (f) call-out, travel, journey, mileage, vehicle, attendance and standby
      charges, save within 7.1.7(g); where nothing billed on an invoice is
      indemnifiable, the attendance charge on that invoice is not indemnifiable
      either. Second attendances, return visits and repeat journeys in respect of
      the same insured event are not reimbursed;

  (g) the same item of cost where it is invoiced more than once in respect of the
      same insured event, whether by one contractor or across several trades;
      only the first such charge is indemnified.

7.1.9 No improvement on the pre-loss standard
Reinstatement proceeds on the basis of the type, quality, grade, format, material
and specification in place immediately before the insured event. Where a higher
specification, a superior material, a greater security rating or a premium range
is chosen instead, indemnity is limited to the cost of an equivalent
standard-grade replacement corresponding to what was in place before the loss;
the difference is borne by the policyholder. Where the pre-existing component is
no longer obtainable, the nearest currently available equivalent of the same grade
sets the ceiling.

7.1.10 Evidence and apportionment
The policyholder demonstrates, for each item and each head of cost claimed, the
affected part or item of insured property to which it relates, the physical damage
established on it, and the making-good purpose the outlay serves. Labour hours,
sundry materials, assembly charges and attendance charges are allocated to the
work they served; where that work is not indemnifiable, they are not
indemnifiable, and where the invoice on which they appear is directed wholly at
property outside Part 4, none of them is indemnified.

Where an invoice line bundles indemnifiable and non-indemnifiable elements and the
elements can be identified and valued from the documents, the line is apportioned.
Where they cannot be separated, the line is assessed by its predominant stated
purpose; where the predominant purpose is not indemnifiable, the line is not
indemnified.

7.2 Market value

Insofar as a building is designated for demolition or otherwise permanently
devalued, insured property is indemnified at the achievable sale price excluding
the land share.

7.3 Construction specification lower or higher than described

Where the actual construction specification at the time of the insured event is of
lower value than described in the contract, the insurer is not obliged to
compensate more than the loss actually incurred. Where it is of higher value, the
indemnity is based on the specification described in the contract.

7.4 Costs

Insured costs under Part 5 are reimbursed where it is demonstrated that they were
actually incurred, and the indemnity limits agreed for each head are applied.

7.5 Loss of rent and rental value

The insurer reimburses the insured loss of rent or rental value up to the end of
the agreed period.

7.6 The reinstatement element of the indemnity

The policyholder acquires a claim to that part of the indemnity which exceeds the
current-value loss only where it ensures that the indemnity will be used to
reinstate or replace insured property of the same kind and intended purpose at the
previous location, and where reinstatement or replacement is secured within three
years of the occurrence of the insured event.

7.7 Value added tax

Value added tax is reimbursed only if and to the extent that it was actually
incurred on the occasion of the reinstatement or replacement, and not where the
policyholder is entitled to recover input tax.

7.8 Deductible

Deductibles are deducted from the indemnity in the amount agreed, once per insured
event.

7.9 When the indemnity falls due

The indemnity falls due once the insurer has conclusively determined the claim as
to its basis and its amount. One month after notifying the loss, the policyholder
may claim as an interim payment the amount that is, on the prevailing assessment,
payable as a minimum. That part of the indemnity which goes beyond the
current-value loss falls due once the policyholder has demonstrated that it has
secured the reinstatement or replacement.

7.10 Repayment of the reinstatement element

The policyholder must repay indemnity paid on the reinstatement basis where,
through its own fault, the property was not reinstated or replaced within a
reasonable period.

7.11 Interest

The indemnity bears interest from the notification of the loss, save where paid
within one month. The rate is [number] percentage point(s) below the applicable
statutory base rate, but at least [percentage] and at most [percentage] per year.

7.12 Suspension of time limits

Any period during which the indemnity cannot be determined or paid owing to the
fault of the policyholder is left out of account.

7.13 Deferral of payment

The insurer may defer payment for as long as there is doubt as to the
policyholder's entitlement to receive payment, official or criminal proceedings
arising out of this insured event are pending, or a legally required involvement
of a secured lender has not taken place.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 8 - EXPERT DETERMINATION PROCEDURE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 After an insured event has occurred, the policyholder may require that the
amount of the loss be determined in an expert determination procedure. Insurer and
policyholder may also agree on such a procedure jointly, and may agree to extend
it to further determinations relating to the insured event.

8.2 Each party nominates one expert in text form. Where a party fails to nominate
within two weeks of a request, the requesting party may have the expert appointed
by the court with local jurisdiction for the loss location. Before beginning their
determinations, the two experts nominate a third expert as umpire.

8.3 The experts' findings must state a schedule of the affected insured property
with the corresponding insurable values; the reinstatement and repair costs; the
residual values; and the insured costs and insured loss of rent or rental value.
Where property outside Part 4 was damaged in the same event, the findings state
the outlay attributable to it separately.

8.4 Each expert transmits its findings to both parties simultaneously. Where the
findings diverge, the umpire decides the points that remain in dispute within the
limits set by the experts' findings. The findings are binding unless they
manifestly deviate substantially from the true state of affairs.

8.5 Unless something else has been agreed, each party bears the costs of its own
expert; the costs of the umpire are borne in equal shares.

8.6 The expert determination procedure does not affect the policyholder's duties.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 9 - POLICYHOLDER DUTIES AND INCREASE IN RISK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.1 Contractually agreed safety requirements before an insured event

9.1.1 Insured property must be kept in proper condition at all times. This applies
in particular to the doors, windows, locks and closing equipment of the building,
to roofs, and to items attached to the exterior. Defects or damage must be
remedied without delay.

9.1.2 When the building or a dwelling within it is left unattended, its doors and
windows must be closed and locked in the customary manner, and the agreed locking
and closing equipment must be kept operational.

9.1.3 Buildings or parts of buildings that are not in use must be inspected
sufficiently frequently at every time of year, and their water-carrying
installations shut off, drained and kept drained.

9.1.4 During the cold season all buildings and parts of buildings must be heated
and checked sufficiently frequently, or their water-carrying installations shut
off, drained and kept drained.

9.2 Duties after an insured event

9.2.1 The policyholder must avert and mitigate the loss so far as can reasonably
be expected, secure the building without delay, and follow the insurer's
instructions where these can be obtained.

9.2.2 The policyholder must report an event under 2.6 without delay to the
competent public authority, notify the insurer without delay, and keep the
affected state unchanged until released.

9.2.3 The policyholder must demonstrate, for each head of cost claimed, the
affected item of insured property to which it relates (7.1.10).

9.3 Consequences of a breach of duty

Where the policyholder breaches one of these duties, and subject to the conditions
set out in the general contract provisions, the insurer is entitled to terminate
the contract and may be wholly or partly released from liability.

9.4 Circumstances constituting an increase in risk

An increase in risk subject to notification may exist in particular where a
circumstance changes about which the insurer asked before the contract was
concluded; where the building or the predominant part of it is no longer in use;
where the agreed locking, closing or security equipment is altered or ceases to be
operational; where construction work renders the building predominantly unusable;
where a commercial operation is taken up or changed within the building; or where
the building is placed under heritage protection after conclusion of the contract.
The consequences of an increase in risk are governed by the general contract
provisions.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 10 - CANCELLATION, SECURED LENDERS, TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

10.1 Cancellation where a security right has been registered

Where a secured lender has registered its charge over the property, cancellation
by the policyholder in respect of the fire peril group is effective only where the
policyholder demonstrated, at least one month before expiry of the insurance
contract, either that the property was no longer encumbered with the charge at the
point at which cancellation was at the latest permissible, or that the secured
lender consented to the cancellation. This does not apply to a cancellation
following a disposal of the property or in the insured event.

10.2 Cancellation after an insured event

After an insured event for which the insurer has rendered a benefit, or has
declined to do so, each party may cancel the contract, observing a notice period
of one month, within one month of the conclusion of the negotiations on the
indemnity. 10.1 remains unaffected.

10.3 Legal position following a transfer of ownership

Where the policyholder disposes of the insured property, the acquirer steps into
its place in the insurance contract at the time of the transfer of ownership; in
the case of real property, at the date of registration in the land register.
Seller and acquirer are jointly and severally liable for the premium for the
insurance period in which the transfer occurs. The insurer need only recognise the
acquirer's entry once it becomes aware of it.

10.4 Rights of cancellation on a transfer of ownership

The insurer may cancel as against the acquirer observing a notice period of one
month; that right lapses if not exercised within one month of the insurer becoming
aware of the disposal. The acquirer may cancel with immediate effect or with
effect from the end of the current insurance period, in text form; that right
lapses one month after acquisition, or one month after the acquirer becomes aware
that the insurance exists. On such a cancellation the seller alone remains liable
for the premium.

10.5 Duties of notification

The disposal must be notified to the insurer without delay in text form by the
seller or the acquirer. Where notification has been omitted, the insurer is not
obliged to pay in the insured event where the event occurred later than one month
after notification ought to have been received and the insurer demonstrates that
it would not have concluded the existing contract with the acquirer. The insurer
remains obliged to pay where it was aware of the disposal, or where the period for
its cancellation had already expired without cancellation at the time of the
insured event.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 11 - LOSS DESCRIPTION AND OPERATIVE PROVISIONS FOR THIS CLAIM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

11.1 A person entered the insured building by force within the meaning of 2.6.1.
The entry point and its locking equipment were damaged and had to be made good and
made secure again. In the course of the same event a movable item kept on the
insured site was damaged; that item is not insured property under this contract
(4.3(b)).

11.2 Invoices were rendered by more than one trade. One is directed at the
building: it comprises the replacement components and hardware, their fitting into
the building, the labour hours of the grades employed on that work, the sundry
materials consumed by it, and the attendance of that trade at the insured
location. The other is directed at the damaged movable item: it comprises the
replacement of assemblies of that item, the labour hours of the grades employed on
it, sundry materials, its assembly, its carriage, and the attendance of that trade.

11.3 The indemnity is determined by asking, for each line, what property the
outlay was directed at. Lines directed at affected insured property are
indemnified under 7.1.7, at every grade of labour, including the sundry materials,
the fitting work and one attendance for the trade concerned. Lines directed at
property outside Part 4 are not indemnified under 7.1.8(a), and neither are the
labour, sundries, assembly, carriage and attendance belonging to them, however
closely their descriptions resemble the indemnifiable lines on the other invoice.

11.4 Clauses 2.6.1, 2.6.2, 2.6.3, 3.1.5, 4.2.3, 4.3(a) to (d), 5.2.1, 6.2.4,
7.1.1, 7.1.5, 7.1.7(a) to (h), 7.1.8(a), 7.1.8(d), 7.1.8(f), 7.1.9, 7.1.10 and 7.8
are the operative provisions for determining how each line of each invoice in this
claim is characterised.

===============================================================================
END OF DOCUMENT

case.policy_digest:
INSURED EVENT: Physical damage caused where a person breaks into, forces open, breaks out of, or attempts by comparable means to enter or leave the insured building, a part of it, or a locked receptacle firmly connected with it (2.6.1).

CONDITIONS OF COVER:
- The property must be insured property under Part 4 (2.6.3, 4.1).
- The loss must be physical damage caused by the break-in event (2.6.1).
- The indemnity is confined to affected parts and items established by the loss investigation (7.1.5).
- The policyholder must demonstrate the affected insured property, established physical damage, and making-good purpose for each claimed item (7.1.10).
- Indemnifiable work must correspond to the pre-loss type, quality, grade, format, material and specification (7.1.9).

LIMITS / SUMS INSURED:
- Destroyed buildings: locally customary reinstatement costs at the time of the insured event (7.1.1(a)).
- Damaged buildings and other insured property: necessary repair costs plus unrepaired diminution in value, capped at the insurable value (7.1.1(b)).
- Price increases are indemnified where reinstatement is secured within three years (7.1.3).
- Reinstatement element requires reinstatement or replacement at the previous location within three years (7.6).
- Emergency and mitigation measures: capped at [amount] per insured event (5.2.1).
- Hotel costs: up to [amount] per day for a maximum of [number] days (5.2.4).
- Early return from holiday: capped at [amount] per insured event (5.2.5).
- Loss of rent or rental value: no longer than [number] months from the occurrence of the insured event (5.4).
- Where a building is permanently devalued, indemnity is the achievable sale price excluding the land share (6.4, 7.2).
- VAT is reimbursed only if actually incurred and not recoverable as input tax (7.7).
- Only one attendance at the insured location by each trade performing indemnifiable work is included (7.1.7(g)).
- Where a pre-existing component is unavailable, the nearest currently available equivalent of the same grade sets the ceiling (7.1.9).

DEDUCTIBLES:
- The deductible is set out in the Schedule and applies once per insured event to the covered settlement (4.7, 7.8).

EXCLUSIONS:
- The taking of property and damage to property not insured under this contract are not indemnified (2.6.3).
- Damage caused by a resident, household employee or entrusted person, unless access was obtained by an act falling within 2.6.1 (2.6.4(a)).
- Damage caused by opening with a key or code properly possessed by the person using it (2.6.4(b)).
- Damage discovered only later and not attributable to an identified event (2.6.4(c)).
- Replacement or upgrading of unaffected locks, hardware or security equipment is not covered (2.6.4(d)).
- Strengthening security beyond the pre-event standard is not covered (2.6.4(d), 7.1.9).
- Property outside Part 4, and every measure directed at it, is outside the contract (3.1.5, 4.3, 7.1.8(a)).
- Maintenance, cleaning, upkeep, modernisation, improvement and renewal of undamaged items are not indemnifiable (3.1.6, 7.1.8(b)).
- Work beyond parts and items affected by the insured event is not covered (3.6, 7.1.5).
- Carriage, freight, delivery, dispatch, packaging, postage, courier and comparable charges are not indemnified (7.1.8(d)).
- Contractor business-operation outlay, including tools, plant, diagnostics, provisioning, catering and administration, is not indemnified (7.1.8(e)).
- Call-out, travel, journey, mileage, vehicle, attendance and standby charges are excluded except within 7.1.7(g); repeat attendances are excluded (7.1.8(f)).
- Duplicate cost items are not reimbursed; only the first such charge is indemnified (7.1.8(g)).
- Higher specifications, superior materials, greater security ratings and premium ranges are limited to equivalent pre-loss standard-grade cost (7.1.9).
- Claims concerning movable household property and personal effects are not insured property (4.3(a), 2.6.3).
- Means of transport and their parts and accessories are not insured property (4.3(b)).
- Sports, leisure, hobby and recreational equipment and their parts and accessories are not insured property (4.3(c)).
- Tools, machines, appliances and equipment for occupants' personal use are not insured property (4.3(d)).
- War, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or insurrection are excluded (3.1.1).
- Internal civil unrest is excluded (3.1.2).
- Nuclear energy, nuclear radiation and radioactive substances are excluded (3.1.3).
- Third-party liability claims and related outlay are excluded (3.1.4).

OBLIGATIONS:
- Keep insured property in proper condition and remedy defects or damage without delay (9.1.1).
- When unattended, close and lock doors and windows customarily and keep agreed equipment operational (9.1.2).
- Inspect unused buildings sufficiently frequently and shut off, drain and keep drained water installations (9.1.3).
- During cold season, heat and check buildings sufficiently frequently, or shut off and drain water installations (9.1.4).
- Avert and mitigate the loss, secure the building without delay, and follow obtainable insurer instructions (9.2.1).
- Report a break-in event without delay to the competent public authority and notify the insurer without delay (9.2.2).
- Keep the affected state unchanged until released (9.2.2).
- Demonstrate the affected insured item for each claimed cost head (9.2.3, 7.1.10).
- Breach may entitle the insurer to terminate and may wholly or partly release it from liability, subject to general contract provisions (9.3).
- Secure reinstatement or replacement within three years to claim the amount exceeding current-value loss (7.6).
- Repay reinstatement-basis indemnity where, through the policyholder's fault, property was not reinstated or replaced within a reasonable period (7.10).
